title: Aussies slugged for woke studies
full_text:
The Albanese government has blown more than $10m of taxpayer funds on what the Coalition has described as a series of “weird, woke and wacky” academic studies — including funding research into “ethical influencers,” AI spirituality, and building resilience against “the reactionary right”.
The projects have been funded as part of the Australian Research Council Future Fellowships program, which provides four-year fellowships to mid-career researchers to undertake “high quality research in areas of national and international benefit”.
However, the Coalition has questioned the merits and cost of some of the projects, including a study being undertaken at Monash University investigating how the “new reactionary right” used “culture” to “build legitimacy and promote anti-democratic politics”.
Other funded projects including a research into “AI-mediated spirituality” with the University of Notre Dame awarded almost $1.5m for the study. The project summary said it would be investigate how AI was “reshaping spiritual practice and belief formation” in Australia.
Another $1.3m was granted to Curtin University to examine “ethical influencers” and how they – including those in Australia and Southeast Asia – defined their own ethics.
A similar amount was awarded to the Australian National University to explore ways in which social justice could be “designed into public spaces, homes and infrastructure” after war while Sydney University received $1.7m for a study looking at how criminal law is used to respond to environmental harm.
The university also received $1.3m for a study into the “ethics” of encouraging families “to have more children than they would otherwise” as part of addressing low fertility rates and almost $1.2m for a project aiming to “accelerate net-zero transport transitions in households with children”.
The uni also received $1.4m for a project examining how international law responded to “feminist critique”, with the project exploring liberal, racial and “ecofeminism” critiques.
Opposition scrutiny of government waste and accountability spokesman Tony Pasin said it was inappropriate for the government to be billing taxpayers for a study to pay an academic to “help them censor ideas they disagree with”.
“This isn’t just weird, woke, and wacky – it’s an extraordinary waste of taxpayer funds,” he said.
“At a time when Australians are paying more for everything because Anthony Albanese and Jim Chalmers can’t manage money, waste like this just makes things worse.” An ARC spokesperson said that project funding applications to the National Competitive Grants Program (NCGP) were subject to “a rigorous and competitive assessment process with the research delivering advances across all fields of knowledge from science, technology and engineering to the humanities and to the social sciences”.
